context: 3.2 Lower Bound for Problem 1 In this section we establish the hardness of Problem 1, at least for combinatorial algorithms3 . The lower bound is based on the known conjecture that combinatorial Boolean matrix multiplication cannot be (polynomial) faster than the naïve algorithm. ▶ Conjecture 11 (Combinatorial Matrix Multiplication, see [12, Conjecture 12]). For any α, β, γ, ε > 0, there is no combinatorial algorithm for multiplying an nα × nβ matrix with an nβ × nγ matrix in time O((nα+β+γ )(1−ε) ) 4 . Based on Conjecture 11 we establish the hardness of Problem 1 even for binary alphabet as follows. ▶ Theorem 12 (Lower bound). Let Q be a combinatorial oracle for Problem 1 for strings over an alphabet Σ with |Σ| ≥ 2. Let p(n, m) and q(n, m) be the preprocessing and query time of Q, respectively. Then there is no ε > 0 such that p(n, m) · q(n, m) = O((nm)1−ε ), unless Conjecture 11 is false.
